execution.description: The miner-signed commitment round trip: Carbon prepares set_commitment, the miner's signer asks on its own terminal and signs, Carbon broadcasts once and reads the digest back; a replay and a second post in the same tempo are refused. It measured the record's call, extension and fee pins.

expected: One round trip measures a positive fee and deposit, and D3's ceiling becomes twice that.
observed: Three heads were needed. The fee account decode read the SDK's raw ss58 bytes as hex (b797bb97). Then set_commitment turned out to be free: fee 0 and both Commitments deposits 0, on the localnet and, read-only, on testnet 567. The signer's record check and the client's answer check both treated a ceiling of 0 as broken (52ba01e5e, 16d41394a). At 1dc22a3c1 it passed: read-back, replay refused, second post refused by the ledger. Testnet 567 composes the same call prefix and the same 13 signed extensions as the localnet.
keep: A measured 0 is a measurement, not a missing value; only null means unmeasured. A ceiling of 0 is the strictest valid ceiling, so it refuses any fee that appears later.
When one guard turns out wrong, grep every boundary that carries the same value (record, signer, client, poster) before handing back a head.
Pins measured on a localnet are checked read-only against the target network before they are committed.
change: If a later runtime starts charging for set_commitment, the zero ceiling refuses every post (FEE_OVER_CEILING) until a new measurement is recorded; that is the intended fail-closed behaviour, not a fault.
